item.title: Prize honors discovery of altermagnetism as a third fundamental class of magnetism
item.description:
📚 Physics News
One of Europe's highest distinctions in condensed matter physics has been awarded for a discovery that is reshaping our understanding of magnetism: The 2026 Europhysics Prize of the European Physical Society (EPS) Condensed Matter Division goes to Professor Jairo Sinova of Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (JGU), Dr. Libor Šmejkal and Professor Tomas Jungwirth for their discovery of altermagnetism—a previously unknown fundamental class of magnetism.

item.title: Interfacial Thermal Conductance Due To Electronic Heat Transport Across A Normal-metal to Superconductor Boundary Of Dissimilar Materials
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Robert Young
Over the course of six decades numerous thermal heat transport measurements across a normal-metal to superconductor interface have shown that attributing this transport exclusively to lattice vibrations (phonons), typically taken proportional to the cube of the temperature ((:T³)), is inadequate. item.title: Electrically driven inverse metamagnetic transition in Sm 1-x Sr x MnO₃
item.description:
📚 Nature Communications
👤 Suryakanta Mondal, Vinod Kumar, Sourav Chowdhury, Akshat Godha, Arup Kumar Mandal, Wan-Sheng Tang 等18位作者
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75886-w Correlated oxides are known to exhibit metamagnetic switching from a non-ferromagnetic to ferromagnetic phase. Here, the authors demonstrate an electrically driven inverse-metamagnetic transition from a ferromagnetic state to an antiferromagnetic-like phase in an epitaxial Sm1-xSrxMnO3 thin film.

item.title: 具有室温磁场驱动180°极化反转的手性Ni2+/Yb3+分子配合物
item.description:

该研究报道一种手性Ni2+/Yb3+分子配合物，其在室温下可由磁场驱动实现180°极化反转。该结果指向分子材料中磁电耦合与可切换极化的新实现路径，具体结构表征、机理分析和性能指标需查阅原文。

item.title: Quantum Zeno effect could freeze computations as qubit systems scale up
item.description:
📚 Physics News
The promise of quantum computing is to solve complex problems faster and more energy-efficiently than today's supercomputers—from optimizing logistics to simulating molecules. This goal is coming within reach as the number of qubits—the computational units of quantum computing—increases.

item.title: Long-lived ytterbium states could sharpen quantum computing and atomic clocks
item.description:
📚 Physics News
Researchers from the University of Amsterdam and the University of New South Wales have answered a question that has been around for decades: whether ions of the metal ytterbium can enter certain long-lived, nearly stable states and, if so, for how long. The measured long-lived states may find applications in quantum computers and atomic clocks.

item.title: Magnetic clues inside atomic nuclei help explain how elements form in stars
item.description:
📚 Physics News
A scientific team led by Facility for Rare Isotope Beams, or FRIB, has identified the origin of a mysterious excess of low-energy gamma rays emitted by the nucleus zinc-70. They found that the excess is caused by magnetic transitions within the nucleus. The study, "Magnetic Character of the Low-Energy Enhancement in 70Zn," published in Nature, sheds light on a long-standing puzzle in nuclear physics and has far-reaching implications for astrophysics.

item.title: Coupled Effects of Boundary Corrugation and Hartmann Damping on Nanofluid Convection in Isosceles Triangular Enclosures: A High-Fidelity Thermophysical Analysis
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Karim Mehrabi
This article presents a high-fidelity numerical investigation of magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) buoyancy-driven transport of an Al2O3-water nanofluid inside a wavy closed isosceles triangular cavity. We employ a customized, non-orthogonal algebraic coordinate transformation mapped onto a custom Discrete Finite Element Method (DFEM) solver to eliminate boundary staircase errors and capture steep localized gradients near the corrugated bottom wall. To address the predictive limits of legacy constant-property models, we implement and contrast two mathematical frameworks: the classical Maxwell-Brinkman formulations and the highly non-linear, temperature-dependent empirical Khanafer-Vafai experimental framework. item.title: Micron-scale Quantum Dot Light-Emitting Diodes with EQE Exceeding 42%
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Hailong Hu, Hao Liu, Kuibao Yu, Tian Liu, Jiahao Wang, Kai Xie 等14位作者
Ultrahigh-resolution quantum dot light-emitting diodes (QLEDs) are promising building blocks for next-generation near-eye micro-displays, yet pixel-edge electric field distortion induces an intrinsic efficiency-resolution trade-off that severely hinders their practical deployment. Tandem architectures enable prominent electroluminescence enhancement, but their implementation in high-resolution patterned QLEDs remains largely unexplored, limited by the inferior charge-generation capability and high operating voltage of conventional charge generation layers (CGLs). item.title: 土耳其埃尔祖鲁姆棕熊胃肠道蠕虫：生物桥梁与人为威胁
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Ridvan Kirman, Muzaffer Akyuz, Salih Dombay, Aybuke Ciplak, Esin Guven, Hamza Avcioglu
研究对土耳其埃尔祖鲁姆四地采集的333份棕熊粪便样本及两只死亡棕熊体内成虫进行显微和分子鉴定。检测到熊蛔虫Baylisascaris transfuga、犬钩口线虫Uncinaria stenocephala和矛形双腔吸虫Dicrocoelium dendriticum，粪样检出率分别为23.4%、3%和19.5%。结果提示棕熊可能作为寄生虫储存宿主，参与病原在环境中的维持及向不同宿主传播，需从“同一健康”视角评估。
